dedupe_keys.name: japan radio station licence search and web api 無線局等情報検索

description: The Japanese Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) publishes the licence information of radio stations in Japan through its Radio Use Portal, to make radio administration transparent and help users study frequency availability. The search covers stations by type, including broadcasting stations for television and radio, mobile base stations, fixed microwave links, amateur and other services, and returns licence details such as licensee, station type, location, frequencies and power; stations related to national security and diplomacy are excluded. A companion REST Web-API lets users query the same system automatically, with one request that counts stations matching conditions and another that returns lists of stations with their licence information, in JSON, XML or CSV; clients must identify themselves in the User-Agent header and accept the API terms of use. The regional communications bureaus also publish open data and statistics, such as counts of broadcast stations and lists of newly opened digital TV relay stations. Coverage: Japan, current licences. Format and access: web search and REST Web-API (JSON, XML, CSV), free after accepting the terms. Caveats: the portal and API pages refused automated requests from this environment, so the fields and terms were not read directly; the precision of station locations was not checked. Simulation uses: inventories of broadcast and mobile transmitter sites for hazard exposure in an earthquake- and typhoon-prone country, and redundancy of broadcast distribution. Related records: the Japanese ministry's 2011 telecom damage record and the QZSS disaster report service cover Japanese resilience, and the FCC LMS database is the US counterpart.
